name: Make Your GPU Earn Its Keep: A Kernel Engineering Deep Dive
description:

**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
A powerful GPU can spend plenty of time waiting. What is it waiting for—and how do you find out?
**Talk #0: Welcome and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth
**Talk #1: From “Why Is This Slow?” to a Faster Kernel**
by Dr. Rajat “Raj” Dandekar, Co-founder of Vizuara
Join Raj for a focused tour of the engineering behind fast AI kernels, drawing on Vizuara’s Kernel Engineering course on Maven. We’ll connect the roofline model to CUDA execution and the GPU memory hierarchy, then look at how profiling guides optimizations such as coalesced memory access, tiling, and tensor-core use. Matrix multiplication and attention provide context for seeing how those ideas fit together in modern AI workloads, including FlashAttention.
The goal is a practical way to decide what to measure, which bottleneck matters, and whether an optimization helped. The session is dedicated to Raj’s talk, with time for audience questions.
**Who it’s for:** Engineers comfortable with Python or basic PyTorch. Prior CUDA or C++ experience is not required.
**Bio:** Dr. Rajat Dandekar is a co-founder of Vizuara and a Kernel Engineering course instructor. He holds a PhD in Mechanical Engineering from Purdue University and BTech and MTech degrees from IIT Madras.
**Based on:** [Kernel Engineering: From CUDA Foundations to Frontier AI Kernels](https://maven.com/rajat-dandekar/kernel-engineering)

name: Hyperledger Fabric for Aerospace Part Traceability: A Doctoral Research Overview
description:
Aircraft parts and components move across airlines, manufacturers, suppliers, and maintenance organizations throughout their service lives. Keeping their maintenance and ownership records accurate and
consistent across these organizations is a continuing challenge, especially when each organization uses different enterprise systems.

In this session, Abhinag Vangala, a doctoral candidate at the University of the Cumberlands, will share an overview of his qualitative research on the use of Hyperledger Fabric for part and component traceability in
multi-organizational environments. The session will cover:

* The traceability challenge in aerospace maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO)
* What prior research has found, and where gaps remain
* Why Hyperledger Fabric was selected for this study
* The study’s three focus areas: system performance, enterprise system integration, and operational suitability

This session may interest Fabric developers, architects, and practitioners who have worked on networks involving multiple organizations.

Abhinag will also share how U.S. based professionals with experience in Hyperledger Fabric or enterprise permissioned blockchain systems can voluntarily take part in the study.

name: DECEMBER GeoDC
description:
**Come out on December 2 for the last GeoDC Event of 2026!**

**As usual, we'll be at SudhouseDC from 6-9pm on the 3rd floor.**

**Arrive between 6-7pm for Networking & Happy Hour Specials.**

**Our program will begin around 7pm with an Upcoming Events & Job Announcements, then we’ll have our featured lightning talks.**

**December Lightning Presentations:**

* **Vanessa Knoppke-Wetzel, ESRI**
**Best Practices for Mapping + AI**
Specifically about production methodology in mapping - the maps we build and create, and the applications, not just data extraction leveraging AI.
Production methodology for mapping has always had mapmakers ask the question: when should I use what technology, method, analysis, and/or design to ensure accuracy and appropriate design while balancing efficiency, and minimizing bias?
Vanessa will share best practices for AI and provide a framework to consider for all mappers to follow in the face of yet another of the ever changing technologies that we face and learn in our mapping journeys (including…. When it to use AI).
* **Nick Mole**
**Historic DC Streetcar Mapping**
This project researches and maps Washington, DC’s streetcar system, from the horse-drawn era through electrification, to build an interactive transit dashboard with a time slider covering 1862 to 1962. Nick will briefly walk through how AI agents were set up to run continuous, repetitive research that builds the project’s archive, and how the geodatabase was designed along with the tools created to clean and review that research and turn it into data. He will also cover the custom tools for drawing the map and for organizing streetcar operators and route relationships by hand. Finally, he will explain how the project was built from the start to fit into OpenHistoricalMap, with its data released to the public domain.
* **Bill Dollins, Cercana Systems**
**Building Provenance, Evidence, and Source Validation into Geospatial AI Systems - Lesson Learned at Clairvoyint**
This talk will explore how we approached building in evidence traceability, source validation, and similar features into the Clairvoyint platform to provide a consistent approach across analytics.

**Feel free to message any of the organizers for questions or suggestions.**

**Tech Talk: Agents That Won’t Quit: Durable Execution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore**
**Speaker:**

* Mark Fussell, Co-founder & CEO, Diagrid
* Yaron Schneider, Co-founder & CTO, Diagrid
* Jean Malha, Principal Specialist Solutions Architect, AWS

**Abstract:** Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gives agents secure, isolated compute, managed identity, memory and access to Bedrock models. Agents that run multi-step tasks over minutes or hours depend on external models, tools and APIs, where timeouts, rate limits, errors and redeployments are a normal part of operating at scale. These agents require durable execution. This session adds Diagrid Catalyst as the agentic durable execution layer on AgentCore, so agent runs complete reliably and every step is verifiable.

With durable execution, an agent interrupted mid-task, by a failed tool call, a timeout or a redeploy, resumes from its last completed step, without re-running completed model calls or tool calls. With verifiable execution, every step is cryptographically signed and traceable to the agent that ran it, producing a tamper-evident record that auditors and risk teams can check. You keep your existing Strands, LangGraph or Mastra code, run on AgentCore and Bedrock, and add one Diagrid package.

**Who should attend**
AI engineers, architects and platform teams building agents on AgentCore and Bedrock, especially teams in regulated industries such as financial services and healthcare that need an auditable record of agent actions.

name: Beyond glue scripts: Orchestrating TF, Ansible, K8s & self-service infra
description:
Every platform team already has the tools: Terraform for infrastructure, Ansible for configuration, Docker and Kubernetes for workloads, Prometheus and Grafana to watch it all. And it already has ways to run workflows around them: cron jobs, Argo Workflows on the cluster, AWX for playbooks, CI pipelines bent into schedulers. Each one works. The problem is that they're spread across tools, so no single place shows what ran, what failed or what depends on what.

This session shows what changes when one orchestrator sits on top of those tools instead. We start with how Kestra runs the Terraform, Ansible and container jobs you already have, versioned in Git and triggered by schedules, events or alerts. Then we build on it to offer self-service provisioning: a request form, an approval, your existing playbook run, and every resource recorded with an owner and an expiry date. A live demo follows one request end to end, and we close with how teams on AWX/AAP bring their existing job templates and playbooks across.

**What you'll learn**
1. How to bring workflows spread across cron, Argo Workflows, AWX and scripts into one orchestrator for Terraform, Ansible, Docker and Kubernetes, versioned in Git.
2. How to turn that automation into self-service provisioning, with approvals, owners and expiry dates.
3. How to bring existing AWX/AAP job templates and playbooks into it without rewriting them.

name: Platform engineering in 2026: What changed, AI agents, and what comes next
description:
In 2025, nearly every platform engineer used AI, but few saw a return. In 2026 that changed. With the State of AI in Platform Engineering Volume 2, the four levels of agentic development, and the State of Platform Engineering Volume 4, the data is in. Agents now open pull requests in nearly a third of organizations, yet only 8% report a major return. We explore what happened and what to expect in 2027.

We break down:
- Where the industry sits on the four levels of agentic software development, and why most organizations stall once agents open pull requests that humans still review by hand
- The four blockers that stand between higher throughput and real ROI, from validation bottlenecks and token costs to agent identity
- How the internal developer platform is evolving into the agentic engineering platform and acting as the foundation of the AI software factory, and what platform teams should build first in 2027

Speaker: Rickey Zachary
Global Engineering Platforms Lead @ Thoughtworks
Rickey Zachary, Global Head of Engineering Platforms at Thoughtworks, specializes in designing and implementing platform engineering solutions that solve enterprise-scale challenges. With over two decades of experience, he helps organizations establish internal developer platforms that increase productivity, reduce cognitive load, and accelerate software delivery. Rickey guides global clients in creating self-service capabilities, implementing platform governance models, and measuring platform effectiveness through DORA and SPACE metrics. His industry recognition includes speaking engagements at major technology conferences like KubeCon, Google Next, and AWS Re:Invent, where he shares insights on platform team structures and operating models. His research in platform standardization, developer portals, and golden paths enables organizations to transform their technical foundations while maintaining the balance between developer autonomy and enterprise governance.

Speaker: Sam Barlien
Head of Ecosystem @ Platform Engineering
Sam Barlien is a researcher at Weave Intelligence, the research arm of platformengineering.org, the world’s largest platform engineering community. With more than 10 years tracking technology communities and ecosystems, he brings first-hand perspective to his research on platform engineering and industry trends. He contributes to Weave Intelligence reports and conducts the weekly research interview series. He co-hosts PlatformCon, the world’s largest platform engineering conference, and contributes to Platform Weekly, the Ambassador program and the platformengineering.org blog.
